meta.description: Batch program that validates and posts daily credit card transactions to the permanent transaction ledger, updating account balances and transaction category balances, while routing invalid transactions to a rejection file.
meta.process_description: CBTRN02C reads each transaction from the daily transaction input file and performs validation checks against the card cross-reference and account master files. Valid transactions are posted to the permanent indexed transaction file and the account balance is updated accordingly, with spending also accumulated by transaction category. Invalid transactions that fail validation are written to a daily rejects file with a reason code and description explaining the failure, and a non-zero return code is set if any rejections occur to alert downstream processes.

files.DALYTRAN: Daily transaction input file – the source feed of credit card transactions to be processed for the current business day
files.TRANFILE: Permanent transaction ledger – the authoritative indexed file where successfully validated and posted transactions are permanently recorded
files.XREFFILE: Card-to-account cross-reference file – maps a credit card number to its associated customer account ID for validation and lookup
files.DALYREJS: Daily rejects output file – captures transactions that failed validation, along with a reason code and description, for investigation and remediation
files.ACCTFILE: Account master file – holds account-level data including current balance, credit limit, and account status; updated when a transaction is posted
files.TCATBALF: Transaction category balance file – maintains running balance totals broken down by account and transaction category/type, used for spending analysis and reporting

business_rules: Every transaction must be validated before posting; a transaction that fails any validation check is never posted to the permanent ledger.
A failed transaction is written to the daily rejects file with a numeric reason code and descriptive text so that operations staff can identify and remediate the problem.
The card number on each transaction must exist in the card-to-account cross-reference file; transactions with an unrecognised card number are rejected.
The resolved account must exist and be in good standing in the account master file; transactions against invalid or non-existent accounts are rejected.
Successfully posted transactions update the account master balance in real time within the batch run, ensuring the account file reflects the day's activity.
Spending is accumulated by transaction category (account + transaction type + category code) in the TCATBAL file; if no category balance record exists yet for that combination, a new one is created.
The batch job sets a return code of 4 if one or more transactions were rejected, enabling job scheduling software to trigger exception handling or alerts.
All files must open successfully before processing begins; any file open failure causes an immediate abnormal termination (ABEND) of the program.
Transaction counts (processed and rejected) are displayed at end of job to provide an audit trail of the batch run's results.

Entry point for the transaction validation routine, called once per transaction read from the daily input file.
Looks up the card number from the transaction against the card-to-account cross-reference file to confirm the card is recognised and retrieve its associated account.
Checks whether the card cross-reference lookup passed without any validation failure; only if the card was successfully recognised does processing continue to the next check.
If the card was valid, proceeds to verify that the associated account exists and is in good standing in the account master file.

If the card was not recognised, skips the account lookup entirely — there is no valid account to check — and allows the already-recorded rejection reason to stand.

Developer note indicating that additional validation rules (e.g. credit limit checks, expiry date checks) should be inserted here as the business requires.

This paragraph validates that the credit card number on an incoming transaction is recognised by the bank's card-to-account cross-reference system. If the card number cannot be found, the transaction is immediately flagged for rejection with a specific reason code and description so operations staff can investigate.
Presents the credit card number from the incoming transaction as the lookup key to search the card-to-account cross-reference file.
Attempts to retrieve the cross-reference record that links this credit card number to its associated customer account.
Begins the handling for the case where the card number does not exist in the cross-reference file.
Marks the transaction as failed with reason code 100, indicating the card number was not recognised by the bank's card registry.
Records a human-readable explanation — 'INVALID CARD NUMBER FOUND' — to accompany the rejection so operations staff understand why the transaction was refused.
Completes writing the rejection description text into the field that will be included in the daily rejects output file.
Begins the handling for the successful case where the card number was found in the cross-reference file.
Confirms that no further action is needed at this stage when the card is valid; processing will continue to the next validation step.
Closes the card cross-reference lookup operation.
Marks the end of this validation step and returns control to the calling paragraph.
Entry point for the account lookup and financial validation step of the transaction validation process.
Uses the account ID resolved from the card cross-reference lookup as the key to retrieve the correct account from the account master file.
Attempts to retrieve the full account record — including balance, credit limit, and expiry date — from the account master file using the resolved account ID.
Handles the case where no matching account record is found in the account master file.
Flags the transaction as rejected with reason code 101, indicating the account does not exist in the master file.
Records a human-readable explanation — 'account record not found' — to be written to the rejects file so operations staff understand why the transaction was declined.
Begins the processing path for transactions where the account was successfully found in the master file.

Calculates a provisional running balance by taking the current cycle's credits, subtracting the current cycle's debits, and adding the amount of the incoming transaction to determine what the balance would be if this transaction were posted.

Checks whether the account's approved credit limit is sufficient to cover the projected balance after posting this transaction — i.e., whether the transaction would cause the account to exceed its credit limit.
If the transaction keeps the account within its credit limit, no action is taken and processing continues to the next validation check.
Flags the transaction as rejected with reason code 102, indicating that posting this transaction would cause the account to exceed its authorised credit limit.
Records a human-readable explanation — 'overlimit transaction' — to be written to the rejects file so operations staff understand the account would be over its credit limit.
Checks whether the account's expiration date is on or after the date the transaction was originally submitted, confirming the account was still active and valid at the time of the transaction.
If the account had not yet expired at the time of the transaction, no action is taken and processing continues.
Flags the transaction as rejected with reason code 103, indicating the transaction was submitted after the account's expiration date.
Records a human-readable explanation — 'transaction received after account expiration' — to be written to the rejects file so operations staff understand the account was no longer valid.
Closes the account file read operation, completing the account lookup and validation block.
Marks the end of this paragraph and returns control to the calling paragraph.

Updates the running spending balance for the relevant account-and-category combination, accumulating this transaction's amount for spending analysis and reporting.

lines.code: * Update the balances in account record to reflect posted trans.

lines.explanation: Applies the transaction amount to the account's current outstanding balance — a purchase increases the balance owed, while a credit or refund reduces it.
Determines whether the transaction represents money being charged to the account (a positive amount) or a credit/refund being applied (a negative amount).
If the transaction is a charge or fee, accumulates its amount into the total credits posted to this account within the current billing cycle.
If the transaction is a refund or payment, accumulates its amount into the total debits applied to this account within the current billing cycle.

Marks the end of this paragraph and returns control to the calling routine if the close succeeded.

Closes the account master file, finalising all balance updates posted during the batch run and releasing the file for other processes.

Confirms the closure was successful by setting the operation status to a healthy/normal state.

Evaluates whether the file closure completed without errors before allowing the program to continue.
No further action needed — the account master file closed successfully, and processing can proceed normally.
Alerts operations staff via the job log that the account master file failed to close, signalling a potential data integrity risk.

Displays the detailed I/O error information to the job log so operations staff can identify the exact nature of the file closure failure.
Triggers an immediate abnormal termination of the batch job to prevent any further processing under an unresolved file error condition.
Marks the end of this routine, returning control to the calling paragraph.

Assumes the worst-case outcome by pre-setting the operation result to a failure state before attempting the close, as a defensive measure.

Checks whether the file system confirmed the transaction category balance file closed successfully without errors.

Marks the end of this paragraph and returns control to the calling routine.

Retrieves the current system date and time from the operating environment as the authoritative moment of processing.
Extracts the four-digit year component from the current date to begin building the formatted timestamp.
Extracts the two-digit month component from the current date for inclusion in the formatted timestamp.

Also checks whether the file status signals a system-level or hardware-related error (status codes beginning with '9' represent OS or physical I/O failures beyond normal application logic).

variables.name: FD-TRAN-RECORD
variables.description: File buffer record for the daily transaction input file (DALYTRAN). Represents one raw credit card transaction as it is physically read from the daily feed before being parsed and validated.

variables.name: FD-TRAN-ID
variables.description: The unique transaction identifier of the incoming daily transaction, used to identify and track this specific credit card event through validation and posting.

variables.name: FD-CUST-DATA
variables.description: The remaining payload of the daily transaction record (card number, amount, merchant details, timestamps, etc.) held as a raw block until mapped into the structured DALYTRAN-RECORD for validation.

variables.name: FD-TRANFILE-REC
variables.description: File buffer record for the permanent transaction ledger (TRANFILE). Represents one posted transaction record as it is written to or read from the authoritative transaction history file.

variables.name: FD-TRANS-ID
variables.description: The unique transaction identifier used as the primary key when writing a validated transaction to the permanent ledger, ensuring each posted transaction can be uniquely retrieved.

variables.name: FD-ACCT-DATA
variables.description: The full transaction detail payload (type, category, amount, merchant, timestamps, etc.) stored alongside the transaction ID in the permanent ledger record.

variables.name: FD-XREFFILE-REC
variables.description: File buffer record for the card-to-account cross-reference file (XREFFILE). Used during validation to look up which customer account is associated with the credit card number on a transaction.

variables.name: FD-XREF-CARD-NUM
variables.description: The credit card number used as the lookup key into the cross-reference file to resolve which account the transaction belongs to. If this card number is not found, the transaction is rejected.

variables.name: FD-XREF-DATA
variables.description: The associated cross-reference data (customer ID and account ID) returned when the card number is found, enabling the program to identify the account to be charged.

variables.name: FD-REJS-RECORD
variables.description: File buffer record for the daily rejects output file (DALYREJS). Represents one rejected transaction entry written out for operations staff to investigate and remediate.

variables.name: FD-REJECT-RECORD
variables.description: The full original transaction record (350 bytes) that failed validation, preserved verbatim in the rejects file so that operations staff have the complete transaction detail for investigation.

variables.name: FD-VALIDATION-TRAILER
variables.description: An 80-byte trailer appended to each rejected transaction record containing the validation failure reason code and its human-readable description, helping operations staff quickly understand why the transaction was rejected.

variables.name: FD-ACCTFILE-REC
variables.description: File buffer record for the account master file (ACCTFILE). Represents one account record read or rewritten during transaction posting, containing the account balance and status that must be validated and updated.

variables.name: FD-ACCT-ID
variables.description: The unique account identifier used as the primary key to locate the correct account master record for balance validation and update when posting a transaction.

variables.name: FD-ACCT-DATA
variables.description: The account detail payload (current balance, credit limit, active status, dates, etc.) associated with the account, read and rewritten when a transaction is posted to reflect the updated balance.

variables.name: FD-TRAN-CAT-BAL-RECORD
variables.description: File buffer record for the transaction category balance file (TCATBALF). Represents one spending-category balance entry that is read and updated (or created) to accumulate transaction amounts by account and spending category.

variables.name: FD-TRAN-CAT-KEY
variables.description: The composite key used to uniquely identify a transaction category balance record, combining account ID, transaction type, and category code to pinpoint the correct spending bucket.

variables.name: FD-TRANCAT-ACCT-ID
variables.description: The account identifier portion of the category balance key, linking the spending total to the specific customer account whose category balance is being accumulated.

variables.name: FD-TRANCAT-TYPE-CD
variables.description: The transaction type code portion of the category balance key (e.g., purchase, cash advance), used to separate spending totals by the nature of the transaction.

variables.name: FD-TRANCAT-CD
variables.description: The transaction category code portion of the category balance key (e.g., groceries, travel, fuel), used to accumulate spending totals within a specific merchant or spending category for analysis and reporting.

variables.name: FD-FD-TRAN-CAT-DATA
variables.description: The running balance and filler data for this account/type/category combination, updated each time a transaction in that spending category is successfully posted.

variables.name: DALYTRAN-STATUS
variables.description: Two-character file status code returned by the operating system after every I/O operation on the daily transaction input file (DALYTRAN), used to detect read errors or end-of-file conditions.

variables.name: DALYTRAN-STAT1
variables.description: The first character of the DALYTRAN file status code; a value of '0' indicates a successful read, '1' indicates end-of-file (no more transactions to process), and other values indicate errors.

variables.name: DALYTRAN-STAT2
variables.description: The second character of the DALYTRAN file status code, providing additional detail about the specific I/O condition encountered when reading the daily transaction feed.

variables.name: TRANFILE-STATUS
variables.description: Two-character file status code returned after every I/O operation on the permanent transaction ledger (TRANFILE), used to confirm that validated transactions were successfully written to the authoritative record.

variables.name: TRANFILE-STAT1
variables.description: The first character of the TRANFILE status code; '0' confirms a successful write to the permanent ledger, while any other value signals a posting failure requiring investigation.

variables.name: TRANFILE-STAT2
variables.description: The second character of the TRANFILE status code, providing granular detail about the specific outcome of the write operation to the permanent transaction ledger.

variables.name: XREFFILE-STATUS
variables.description: Two-character file status code returned after every I/O operation on the card-to-account cross-reference file (XREFFILE), used to determine whether a card number lookup succeeded or the card is unrecognised.

variables.name: XREFFILE-STAT1
variables.description: The first character of the XREFFILE status code; '0' means the card number was found and the account ID was resolved, while '2' (record not found) triggers rejection of the transaction.

variables.name: XREFFILE-STAT2
variables.description: The second character of the XREFFILE status code, providing additional detail about the card number lookup result in the cross-reference file.

variables.name: DALYREJS-STATUS
variables.description: Two-character file status code returned after every write operation to the daily rejects file (DALYREJS), used to confirm that failed transactions and their rejection reasons were successfully captured for operations review.

variables.name: DALYREJS-STAT1
variables.description: The first character of the DALYREJS status code; '0' confirms the rejected transaction record was successfully written to the rejects file for remediation.

variables.name: DALYREJS-STAT2
variables.description: The second character of the DALYREJS status code, providing granular detail about the outcome of writing a rejected transaction to the rejects file.

variables.name: ACCTFILE-STATUS
variables.description: Two-character file status code returned after every I/O operation on the account master file (ACCTFILE), used to confirm successful account lookups and balance updates during transaction posting.

variables.name: ACCTFILE-STAT1
variables.description: The first character of the ACCTFILE status code; '0' confirms the account was found and updated successfully, while other values indicate the account does not exist or the update failed, triggering rejection.

variables.name: ACCTFILE-STAT2
variables.description: The second character of the ACCTFILE status code, providing additional detail about the specific outcome of the account master file read or rewrite operation.

variables.name: TCATBALF-STATUS
variables.description: Two-character file status code returned after every I/O operation on the transaction category balance file (TCATBALF), used to determine whether an existing category balance record was found (to be updated) or is absent (requiring creation).

variables.name: TCATBALF-STAT1
variables.description: The first character of the TCATBALF status code; '0' means an existing spending-category balance record was found and will be updated, while '2' (not found) means a new category balance record must be created for this account/type/category combination.

variables.name: TCATBALF-STAT2
variables.description: The second character of the TCATBALF status code, providing granular detail about the specific outcome of the category balance file read or write operation.

variables.name: IO-STATUS
variables.description: General-purpose two-character I/O status work area used to consolidate and evaluate file status codes across all files, supporting centralised error handling and ABEND logic when a critical file operation fails.

variables.name: IO-STAT1
variables.description: The first character of the general I/O status, indicating the broad category of the file operation result (success, end-of-file, or error) for the most recently checked file.

variables.name: IO-STAT2
variables.description: The second character of the general I/O status, providing the specific sub-code for the file operation result, used in error messages and ABEND decisions.

variables.name: TWO-BYTES-BINARY
variables.description: A two-byte binary work field used to convert a numeric file status code into its individual character bytes, enabling the program to inspect and display I/O status values in error reporting.

variables.name: TWO-BYTES-ALPHA
variables.description: An alphanumeric overlay of the TWO-BYTES-BINARY field, allowing the same two bytes to be read as individual characters for constructing human-readable I/O status codes in error messages and logs.

variables.name: TWO-BYTES-LEFT
variables.description: The left (first) character byte of the binary status field overlay, corresponding to the first digit of the file status code used in error diagnosis.

variables.name: TWO-BYTES-RIGHT
variables.description: The right (second) character byte of the binary status field overlay, corresponding to the second digit of the file status code used in error diagnosis.

variables.name: IO-STATUS-04
variables.description: A structured work area used to decompose and display a four-digit I/O status code in error messages, helping operations staff pinpoint the exact file system error that caused a processing failure.

variables.name: IO-STATUS-0401
variables.description: The leading single digit of the expanded I/O status code, representing the primary status category (e.g., 0=success, 1=end-of-file, 2=invalid key, 3=permanent error) for error reporting.

variables.name: IO-STATUS-0403
variables.description: The trailing three digits of the expanded I/O status code, providing the detailed sub-status for precise identification of the file error condition in operations logs and ABEND messages.

variables.name: APPL-RESULT
variables.description: A numeric result code returned from called sub-routines or system services, used to determine whether an operation (such as a file I/O or utility call) completed successfully or encountered an error requiring special handling.

variables.name: APPL-AOK
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when the last application operation completed successfully (result code = 0), allowing the program to proceed with normal transaction processing.

variables.name: APPL-EOF
variables.description: Condition name that evaluates to true when the last application operation returned an end-of-file condition (result code = 16), signalling that all daily transactions have been read and the main processing loop should terminate.

variables.name: END-OF-FILE
variables.description: A flag that controls the main transaction processing loop. Initialised to 'N' (not finished); set to 'Y' when the daily transaction input file is exhausted, causing the program to stop reading transactions and proceed to end-of-job reporting.

variables.name: ABCODE
variables.description: The abnormal termination (ABEND) code passed to the operating system when a fatal error occurs (such as a file open failure), identifying the specific cause of the unplanned job termination for operations and support staff.

variables.name: TIMING
variables.description: A binary work field used to capture elapsed time or timing measurements during the batch run, supporting performance monitoring and SLA compliance reporting for the daily transaction posting job.

variables.name: COBOL-TS
variables.description: A structured timestamp work area used to capture and format the current date and time, typically stamped onto transaction records or log messages to provide an audit trail of when processing occurred.

variables.name: COB-YYYY
variables.description: The four-digit year component of the processing timestamp, used when recording the date a transaction was processed or when generating audit log entries.

variables.name: COB-MM
variables.description: The two-digit month component of the processing timestamp, used together with the year and day to form a complete processing date for audit and reconciliation purposes.

variables.name: COB-DD
variables.description: The two-digit day component of the processing timestamp, identifying the specific calendar day on which the batch transaction posting run executed.

variables.name: COB-HH
variables.description: The two-digit hour component of the processing timestamp, providing time-of-day precision in audit records to support intra-day reconciliation and SLA tracking for the batch posting job.

variables.name: COB-MIN
variables.description: The minutes component of the current system time, used when constructing a formatted timestamp to record when a transaction was processed or when a reject was logged.

variables.name: COB-SS
variables.description: The seconds component of the current system time, used when building a precise processing timestamp to be stamped on transaction or reject records.

variables.name: COB-MIL
variables.description: The hundredths-of-a-second (milliseconds) component of the current system time, providing sub-second precision in the processing timestamp attached to each transaction record.

variables.name: COB-REST
variables.description: Overflow or trailing portion of the COBOL system time value that is not directly used in the formatted timestamp but is captured to fully consume the system time field and avoid data truncation.

variables.name: DB2-FORMAT-TS
variables.description: A 26-character timestamp string formatted in DB2/ISO standard (YYYY-MM-DD-HH.MM.SS.xx) that records the exact date and time a transaction was processed. This timestamp is written to the permanent transaction ledger (TRANFILE) and the rejects file (DALYREJS) to provide a precise, auditable record of when each transaction was handled by the batch job.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A group-level overlay of the DB2-FORMAT-TS timestamp field that breaks the single 26-character string into individually addressable date and time components (year, month, day, hour, minute, second, millisecond). This allows the program to assemble or inspect each part of the processing timestamp separately before writing it to transaction or reject records.

variables.name: DB2-YYYY
variables.description: The four-digit year portion of the DB2-formatted processing timestamp (e.g., '2024'), ensuring the transaction processing date is recorded in a century-unambiguous format on all ledger and reject records.

variables.name: DB2-STREEP-1
variables.description: The first separator character (a hyphen '-') in the DB2 timestamp format, placed between the year and month components to produce the standard YYYY-MM-DD date representation on transaction records.

variables.name: DB2-MM
variables.description: The two-digit month portion of the DB2-formatted processing timestamp (e.g., '07' for July), identifying the calendar month in which the transaction was processed and recorded.

variables.name: DB2-STREEP-2
variables.description: The second separator character (a hyphen '-') in the DB2 timestamp format, placed between the month and day components to maintain the standard date format on all transaction and reject records.

variables.name: DB2-DD
variables.description: The two-digit day-of-month portion of the DB2-formatted processing timestamp (e.g., '19'), pinpointing the exact calendar day on which the batch processed and posted or rejected each transaction.

variables.name: DB2-STREEP-3
variables.description: The third separator character (a hyphen '-') in the DB2 timestamp format, placed between the date and time portions to delimit the day from the hour in the standard DB2 timestamp layout.

variables.name: DB2-HH
variables.description: The two-digit hour component (24-hour clock) of the DB2-formatted processing timestamp, recording the hour of day at which the batch job processed the transaction, supporting precise audit trail requirements.

variables.name: DB2-DOT-1
variables.description: The first dot separator character in the time portion of the DB2 timestamp (between hours and minutes), conforming to the DB2 timestamp format HH.MM.SS used on all posted and rejected transaction records.

variables.name: DB2-MIN
variables.description: The two-digit minutes component of the DB2-formatted processing timestamp, providing minute-level precision in the audit timestamp written to the transaction ledger and rejects file.

variables.name: DB2-DOT-2
variables.description: The second dot separator character in the time portion of the DB2 timestamp (between minutes and seconds), maintaining the standard DB2 time format on all transaction processing records.

variables.name: DB2-SS
variables.description: The two-digit seconds component of the DB2-formatted processing timestamp, providing second-level precision in the audit trail timestamp recorded against each posted or rejected transaction.

variables.name: DB2-DOT-3
variables.description: The third dot separator character in the DB2 timestamp (between seconds and milliseconds), completing the standard DB2 timestamp format HH.MM.SS.xx on all transaction records.

variables.name: DB2-MIL
variables.description: The two-digit hundredths-of-a-second (sub-second) component of the DB2-formatted processing timestamp, providing the finest level of time precision in the audit timestamp to distinguish transactions processed within the same second.

variables.name: DB2-REST
variables.description: Trailing filler characters at the end of the DB2 timestamp overlay that absorb any remaining bytes of the 26-character timestamp field not occupied by the named date/time components, ensuring the full field length is accounted for without data corruption.

variables.name: REJECT-RECORD
variables.description: The complete output record written to the daily rejects file (DALYREJS) for every transaction that fails validation. It combines the full original transaction data with a validation trailer so that operations staff have both the transaction details and the specific reason for rejection in a single record for investigation and remediation.

variables.name: REJECT-TRAN-DATA
variables.description: The complete, verbatim copy of the original daily transaction record (350 bytes, matching the DALYTRAN-RECORD layout) that failed validation. Preserving the full transaction data in the reject record allows operations staff to see exactly what was submitted and attempt reprocessing or manual correction.

variables.name: VALIDATION-TRAILER
variables.description: An 80-character suffix appended to each reject record containing the numeric rejection reason code and its human-readable description. This trailer tells operations staff precisely why the transaction was refused (e.g., unrecognised card number, invalid account), enabling targeted investigation and remediation without needing to re-run the batch.

variables.name: WS-VALIDATION-TRAILER
variables.description: A working-storage group record used to build the validation failure information before it is moved into the VALIDATION-TRAILER field of the reject record. It structures the rejection reason code and description as separate, addressable fields so the program can set them independently during validation checks.

variables.name: WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON
variables.description: A four-digit numeric code that identifies the specific business rule that a transaction violated, causing it to be rejected. A value of zero means the transaction passed all validations. Non-zero values (e.g., unrecognised card number, inactive account) are written to the rejects file so operations staff can categorise and prioritise remediation work.

variables.name: WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON-DESC
variables.description: A plain-English description of why a transaction was rejected (e.g., 'Card number not found in cross-reference file'), written alongside the numeric reason code in the rejects file. This human-readable text allows operations staff to immediately understand the problem without needing to look up a code table.

variables.name: WS-COUNTERS
variables.description: A group of working-storage accumulators that track the volume and financial outcomes of the batch run. These counters are displayed at end-of-job to provide an audit trail showing how many transactions were attempted, how many were rejected, and what balance calculations were performed.

variables.name: WS-TRANSACTION-COUNT
variables.description: A running total of every transaction read from the daily input file (DALYTRAN) during the batch run, regardless of whether it passed or failed validation. Displayed at end-of-job, this count confirms how many transactions the business submitted for processing that day and forms the top-line figure of the batch audit trail.

variables.name: WS-REJECT-COUNT
variables.description: A running total of transactions that failed one or more validation checks and were written to the daily rejects file (DALYREJS) instead of being posted to the permanent ledger. Displayed at end-of-job and used to set the job return code to 4 when non-zero, alerting operations that exceptions require attention.

variables.name: WS-TEMP-BAL
variables.description: A temporary working balance used during the account balance update step when posting a valid transaction. The transaction amount is applied to this field first before the result is written back to the account master record (ACCTFILE), protecting the stored balance from partial updates if an error occurs mid-calculation.

variables.name: WS-FLAGS
variables.description: A group of working-storage flag fields that control processing decisions during the batch run, such as whether to create new records or update existing ones in the various output files.

variables.name: WS-CREATE-TRANCAT-REC
variables.description: A flag that controls whether the program must create a brand-new transaction category balance record in the TCATBAL file ('Y') or simply update an existing one ('N') for the current transaction's account-type-category combination. Set to 'Y' when a cardholder makes a purchase in a spending category that has never been recorded before for their account, triggering the creation of a new category balance entry to track that type of spending going forward.

paragraphs.name: 0000-DALYTRAN-OPEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph opens the daily transaction input file before any processing begins, ensuring the batch job has access to the day's credit card transactions. If the file cannot be opened, the program immediately terminates abnormally to prevent any processing from occurring without a valid transaction source.

paragraphs.name: 0100-TRANFILE-OPEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph opens the permanent transaction ledger file for writing, ready to receive validated transactions. If the file cannot be opened, the batch job immediately terminates abnormally, preventing any processing from occurring without a reliable destination for posted transactions.

paragraphs.name: 0200-XREFFILE-OPEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph opens the card-to-account cross-reference file, which is essential for resolving credit card numbers to customer accounts during transaction validation. If the file cannot be opened successfully, the batch job immediately terminates abnormally, as processing cannot safely continue without this critical lookup resource.

paragraphs.name: 0300-DALYREJS-OPEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph opens the daily rejects output file so that any transactions failing validation can be captured and written for investigation. If the file cannot be opened, the batch job immediately terminates abnormally, as the ability to record rejected transactions is a mandatory prerequisite for safe processing.

paragraphs.name: 0400-ACCTFILE-OPEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph opens the account master file in read/write mode so that account balances can be both retrieved and updated during transaction posting. If the file cannot be opened successfully, the batch job immediately terminates abnormally, as processing cannot safely continue without access to account data.

paragraphs.name: 0500-TCATBALF-OPEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph opens the transaction category balance file in read/write mode so that spending totals by account and category can be both read and updated during the batch run. If the file cannot be opened, the program immediately abends to prevent any processing from occurring without access to this critical file.

paragraphs.name: 1000-DALYTRAN-GET-NEXT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph retrieves the next credit card transaction from the daily input feed for processing. It handles three outcomes: a successful read, a clean end-of-file signal, or an unexpected I/O error that forces an immediate halt.

paragraphs.name: 1500-VALIDATE-TRAN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph orchestrates the full validation sequence for each incoming credit card transaction before it can be posted to the permanent ledger. It runs each required validation check in order, stopping further checks only when a failure has already been detected, ensuring no invalid transaction is ever posted.

paragraphs.name: 1500-A-LOOKUP-XREF
paragraphs.description: This paragraph validates that the credit card number on an incoming transaction is recognised by the bank's card-to-account cross-reference system. If the card number cannot be found, the transaction is immediately flagged for rejection with a specific reason code and description so operations staff can investigate.

paragraphs.name: 1500-B-LOOKUP-ACCT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph retrieves the account record associated with the resolved account ID and performs two critical financial validations: confirming the account exists, checking that the transaction would not push the account over its credit limit, and verifying the account has not expired. Any failure is recorded with a specific rejection reason so operations staff can investigate.

paragraphs.name: 2000-POST-TRANSACTION
paragraphs.description: This paragraph orchestrates the full posting of a validated credit card transaction to the bank's permanent records. It assembles the complete transaction detail, updates spending category balances, adjusts the account balance, and writes the transaction to the authoritative ledger.

paragraphs.name: 2500-WRITE-REJECT-REC
paragraphs.description: This paragraph writes a failed transaction to the daily rejects file, bundling the original transaction data with the rejection reason so that operations staff can investigate and remediate the failure. If the write to the rejects file itself fails, the program immediately abends to prevent silent data loss.

paragraphs.name: 2700-UPDATE-TCATBAL
paragraphs.description: This paragraph maintains the running spending balance for the account's specific transaction category by either updating an existing category balance record or creating a new one if this is the first transaction of that type for the account. It ensures that every posted transaction is correctly reflected in the category-level spending totals used for analysis and reporting.

paragraphs.name: 2700-A-CREATE-TCATBAL-REC
paragraphs.description: Creates a brand-new transaction category balance record for a specific account, transaction type, and spending category combination that does not yet exist in the category balance file. This establishes the initial spending baseline for that category so future transactions can accumulate against it.

paragraphs.name: 2700-B-UPDATE-TCATBAL-REC
paragraphs.description: This paragraph updates the running spending balance for the current transaction's category by adding the transaction amount to the existing category total and saving the result back to the category balance file. It ensures that per-category spending totals remain accurate after each posted transaction, and abends the job immediately if the file update fails to protect data integrity.

paragraphs.name: 2800-UPDATE-ACCOUNT-REC
paragraphs.description: This paragraph applies a validated transaction to the account master record by updating the current balance and the appropriate cycle-to-date credit or debit accumulator, then permanently saves the updated account back to the account master file. It ensures the account's financial position accurately reflects all transactions posted during the batch run.

paragraphs.name: 2900-WRITE-TRANSACTION-FILE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph permanently records a validated credit card transaction into the authoritative transaction ledger. If the write operation fails for any reason, the batch job is immediately halted to prevent data integrity issues in the permanent record.

paragraphs.name: 9000-DALYTRAN-CLOSE
paragraphs.description: Safely closes the daily transaction input file after all transactions have been read and processed for the business day. Any failure to close the file cleanly triggers an immediate abnormal termination to protect data integrity and alert operations staff.

paragraphs.name: 9100-TRANFILE-CLOSE
paragraphs.description: Safely closes the permanent transaction ledger at the end of the batch run, ensuring all posted transactions are flushed and committed to the file. If the ledger cannot be closed cleanly, the program halts immediately to prevent data corruption or an incomplete audit trail.

paragraphs.name: 9200-XREFFILE-CLOSE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph safely closes the card-to-account cross-reference file after all transaction lookups are complete. If the file cannot be closed cleanly, the batch job is immediately terminated to protect data integrity and alert operations staff.

paragraphs.name: 9300-DALYREJS-CLOSE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph safely closes the daily rejects output file at the end of the batch run, ensuring all rejected transaction records are fully flushed and persisted to disk. If the file cannot be closed cleanly, the program halts immediately to prevent data loss or corruption of the rejection audit trail.

paragraphs.name: 9400-ACCTFILE-CLOSE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph safely closes the account master file at the end of the batch run, ensuring all posted balance updates are properly flushed and the file is released. If the file cannot be closed cleanly, the program immediately abends to prevent data corruption or incomplete updates from going undetected.

paragraphs.name: 9500-TCATBALF-CLOSE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph safely closes the transaction category balance file at the end of the batch run, ensuring all accumulated spending-by-category totals are properly flushed and saved. If the file cannot be closed cleanly, the program halts immediately to prevent data corruption or incomplete category balance records.

paragraphs.name: Z-GET-DB2-FORMAT-TIMESTAMP
paragraphs.description: This paragraph captures the current system date and time and formats it into a standardised database-compatible timestamp. This timestamp is used to record the precise moment a transaction or ledger entry is created, providing an accurate audit trail for all posted activity.

paragraphs.name: 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM
paragraphs.description: This paragraph performs an immediate, controlled abnormal termination of the batch job when a catastrophic error is encountered (such as a file failing to open), ensuring the failure is clearly signalled to operations and the job scheduler rather than allowing the program to continue in an undefined state.

paragraphs.name: 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph formats and displays a human-readable file status code to the job log whenever a file I/O error occurs, enabling operations staff and support teams to diagnose exactly which file operation failed and why during the batch run.
